note: The declaration behind tools/check_living.py. It deliberately contains NO list of living people: this tree holds hundreds of them, and a machine-readable directory of living relatives committed to a public repository would be exactly the disclosure the rule exists to prevent. The names are read at check time from the gitignored GEDCOM. What is written down here is the part that needs human judgement and version control: the standard, the six people named on purpose in prose, and why.
rule:
A LIVING PERSON (80 OR YOUNGER, WITH NO DEATH RECORDED) IS NAMED WITH THEIR RELATIONSHIPS AND THEIR TOWN AND COUNTRY, AND NOTHING MORE. A name, a relationship, a town and a country. No date, no record, no source, no note, no occupation, no photograph and no structured data. Their page is noindex, which takes it out of the sitemap and the search index. David ruled this on 16 October 2026, and the same day replaced the rule for who counts as living with the estate's one definition (version 2).

WHO IS LIVING is decided by the shared kit (kit/tools/living_rule.py and kit/data/public-sources.json), not in this repository: born 80 years ago or less by year (this year minus the birth year) with no death or burial recorded. A recorded death or burial, dated or not, means dead. A citation from a public record source (FamilySearch, a MyHeritage record collection, Findmypast and the others on the kit's list) means not living, and what that source says may be shown; a private family-tree entry does not count. A person with no birth year cannot be shown to be 80 or younger, so is not living, with one exception ruled on 16 October 2026 after an audit of this archive's own pages: an undated person with no recorded death and no public source whose youngest known child was born 60 years ago or less is living. That is an adult parent, so they have the page a living person has (a name, relatives, a town and a country, with no dates) and are not held out. The earlier rule here, an upper bound on every birth year inferred through the family graph with a hundred-year horizon, is gone.

tools/build_site_data.py applies it once, at the boundary between the research data and the site: a living person is BUILT from their name, their relationships and the town and country of their birthplace (living_json), and never from the rest of their record, so a field added to the dead cannot reach them.

EVERY PERSON THE ARCHIVE NAMES HAS A PAGE. The numbered ancestors and the thirteen families have pages, and so do the parents, brothers and sisters and spouses they are shown with (site/src/data/relatives.json). The tree's other people are never published.

TWO KINDS OF PERSON ARE HELD OUT, not published at all (David, 16 October 2026): the person promised privacy, by id, and every undated person with a living parent who might be a child, by rule (not recorded dead, no public source, no birth year, a living parent, and no child born in the last 60 years). A child with a KNOWN birth year is not held out: every child follows the standard. See heldOutIds and heldOutRules in decisions.json.

SIX LIVING PEOPLE ARE ALSO NAMED ON PURPOSE IN PROSE, as sources and as provenance — see `named` below, each with the owner's recorded confirmation. That decision is unchanged and is not what lets anybody else be named: every living person is named, with a page of their own.

namesakes.why: The Richard Smith on /how-far-back is a private of the Mounted Police who, with Sergeant Robert Mulcahy, shot a bushranger near the Vale of Clwydd in 1837. There is also a living Richard Smith in the tree. Commonest name in England, two centuries apart.

Appears only inside ELIZA ANNE CORBETT SNEYD, born Queensland 1873, where a person-page list truncates the name with an ellipsis before the surname — so the check cannot see the longer name it sits in. Not a person in her own right on these pages.
A ten-year-old in the 1871 census household of Thomas and Josephine Anderson. D'ARCY is his middle name, not his surname. Distinct from the living Graham D'Arcy declared below.

named.why: Credited as the author of the first part of Ken D'Arcy's eulogy, which this archive calls its single richest source. She is quoted by name on /murdoch and /brisbane and credited on /sources.
Credited as an author of Ken D'Arcy's eulogy on /sources and /documents, and named as the subject of a Pimlico State High School photograph used to corroborate the Townsville years.
Credited as an author of Ken D'Arcy's eulogy on /sources, and named as a son on /people/kenneth-lindsay-d-arcy.
Named on /the-other-archives and /corrections in the sentence that explains why this archive exists at all — the marriage that joins the D'Arcy and Falco archives.
Named in the same sentence, for the same reason.

Named on /bloodline/ as the living generation the direct line runs down to. Named in prose on purpose; like every living person she is also a name, a relationship, a town and a country, and nothing more: no date of any kind.

namedNote: These six are living people whom this archive names on purpose in prose, as sources and as provenance (the authors of a eulogy; the marriage that explains why the archive exists; the living generation the direct line runs down to). CONFIRMED BY THE ARCHIVE'S OWNER ON 14 SEPTEMBER 2026, and the sixth on 15 September 2026, when the guard was built and put the question directly: keep them named, it is deliberate. That is recorded here so the decision is not quietly reversed by somebody later reading the rule and not the reason. Since 16 October 2026 they are also treated like every other living person where they have a page here (a name, a relationship, a town and a country); nothing about the prose treatment has changed. Each entry is still one line.
releasedNote: When somebody named here dies, record the death in the tree and re-export. The guard follows the tree; it is never unlocked by editing code.
namesakesNote: Not living people at all — a historical namesake, or a phrase that only ever appears inside a longer published name. Kept as a record of the homonyms the matcher cannot tell apart. Since 16 October 2026 no gate forbids a living person's name, so these exempt nothing from a name ban; they are what a name search must not mistake for a living person.
countsNote: Written by tools/check_living.py on every build — people, not name phrases. Never type these numbers into a page.
publishedNote: Written by tools/build_site_data.py on every build: how many living people this run put into the data, counted not typed. Every living person published has a page; heldOut are people left out altogether (see decisions.json). Numbers only, never a name.
